newsitem.title: USA: U.S. disclosure rule on lead paint takes effect.
newsitem.headline: U.S. disclosure rule on lead paint takes effect.

text.p: Home buyers and tenants have the right to know about potential lead-based paint hazards before they buy or rent older housing effective Friday, the Environmental Protection Agency said.
"Today, we guarantee for the first time that all home buyers have the right to know about hazardous lead paint in their homes," EPA Administrator Carol Browner said in a statement.
"Today's action will greatly contribute to our efforts to prevent and eliminate the incidence of childhood lead poisoning nationwide," she said.

With the rule, prospective tenants or buyers of housing built before 1978, including single-family home owners, will have the right to demand information on known lead-based paint and lead-based paint hazards in the building before buying or renting.
Prospective buyers or renters also will get a short pamphlet on basic lead-poisoning prevention tips.
The first phase of the joint EPA-Housing Department programme took effect Sept. 6, when owners with more than four residential dwellings and their agents were required to disclose known hazards.

More than 1.7 million Americans under the age of 6 have unsafe blood lead levels, which may lead to lowered intelligence ratings, reading and learning disabilities, impaired hearing and other problems, the EPA said.
